extracted.intended_audience: Faculty, administrators, librarians, and staff at US higher-education institutions (including community colleges, tribal colleges, HBCUs, liberal arts colleges, teachers' colleges, and research universities) interested in applying for the HuMetricsHSS Community Fellowship.
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of an application to the HuMetricsHSS Community Fellowship proposing values-based changes to institutional metrics and academic culture; applications are evaluated for potential institutional impact, community-building, and communicability/adaptability. Includes eligibility, required materials, deadlines, and funding details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (who may apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellows Program is open to contingent, full-time, and tenure-line faculty, administrators, librarians, and staff from any US-based institution of higher education, including community colleges, tribal colleges, HBCUs, liberal arts colleges, and teachers’ colleges, as well as the entire range of research universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may be individual or collaborative; for purposes of selection only one person should serve as the corresponding applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project fit / purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are individuals who are engaged in transforming academic culture at their own institutions, whether by rethinking what forms of scholarship 'count,' considering how indicators and metrics might be informed by values, or engaging their communities in values-inflected ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HuMetricsHSS facilitates creation of locally relevant values-based frameworks that enable scholars in HSS, departments, and institutions to tell more textured and compelling stories about the impact of their research and the variety of ways it enriches public life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be prepared to provide their title, institutional affiliation, and current role; a brief description of their current engagement with values-based practices; a brief description of the institutional change they intend to undertake; and the names and contact information for any collaborators (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are submitted through the SSRC Application Portal (create login/password). You may begin, save, and return to complete the proposal before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: potential for real change at home institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will be evaluated according to the potential for the Fellow(s) to make real change at their home institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is listed as one of several principles (in no particular order) that reviewers will apply when making funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: plan for fostering a community of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will be evaluated according to the plan for fostering a community of practice around this work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for concrete strategies to build and sustain a community engaged with values-based metrics and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion: communication and reusability of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will be evaluated according to the plan for the Fellow(s) to communicate their work and the potential for others to learn from and adapt/continue/build on that work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on clarity of dissemination and likelihood that outcomes will be transferable or scalable to other contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated capacity to drive institutional adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The successful applicant will demonstrate their interest in and their ability to drive institutional adoption of the HuMetricsHSS values-enacted approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide evidence or a plausible plan showing they can influence institutional practices or policies (e.g., past work, partnerships, formal roles, or concrete next steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget/funding terms and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Each HuMetricsHSS Fellow or collaborative team will receive a one-time stipend of $4500 for use over the course of the fifteen-month fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award amount is the same regardless of the number of collaborators and is allocated for the Fellow’s discretionary use within their home institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadline and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed applications must be submitted by Friday, October 22, 2021.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications open 9/22/2021 and decisions will be made by the HuMetricsHSS Initiative team alongside a small panel of peer reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding decisions will be made by members of the HuMetricsHSS Initiative team alongside a small panel of peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are evaluated according to the stated principles (potential for institutional change, community-building plan, communication/adaptability plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural rule: single corresponding applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The HuMetricsHSS Community Fellowship is open to both individual and collaborative applications, but we ask that only one person serve as corresponding applicant for the purposes of selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the application designates a single corresponding applicant even for collaborative teams.
